hypotheses.justification: The conclusion holds for every integer matrix. Reachable means a nonempty type of walks; using Walk.getVert and diagramGraph_adj gives a finite sequence with the required endpoints and consecutive nonzero entries. Choose such a sequence of minimum length using Nat.find, without requiring its steps to remain diagram edges. Repeated vertices would allow deleting a loop, contradicting minimality, so the sequence is injective on its index interval. Any nonzero A (w i) (w j) with i + 1 < j ≤ n would allow replacing that segment by one step, again contradicting minimality. Thus all required forward nonconsecutive entries vanish, even for asymmetric matrices. When u = v, length zero and the constant sequence suffice; an empty B cannot supply the endpoints. No finite-type assumption is needed.
